description: Internet Society Pulse, launched in December 2020 as part of the Internet Society's Measuring the Internet project, consolidates trusted third-party internet measurement data into one platform and adds its own curated datasets. Its main products are a tracker of internet shutdowns (973 intentional total or partial disruptions tracked since 2019 as of 26 September 2026, each with country, dates, scope, duration and a confidence grade from suspected to confirmed), the Internet Resilience Index, which scores 179 countries and territories out of 100 on infrastructure, affordability, performance and market readiness (overall score 56 for January 2026), an IXP tracker, and indicators on the adoption of enabling technologies such as IPv6, HTTPS and DNSSEC and on market concentration. The Internet Society publishes it so that policymakers, researchers, journalists, network operators and civil society can understand the availability, reliability and resilience of local and global internet infrastructure. Coverage is global by country, from 2019 for shutdowns and monthly for the index. Data can be browsed and charted on the site, and the Pulse API gives programmatic access with a free account and API key. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): Internet Society Pulse Terms and Conditions (Pulse Data may be used, copied and published for non-commercial purposes; no resale or redistribution). Caveats: the resilience index is a weighted composite whose weights shape rankings; shutdown records rely on measurement and media evidence and some remain unconfirmed; partner data vary in method and coverage. Simulation uses: country-level resilience indicators and historical disruption events for resilience, emergency-response and scenario studies of communications. Related records: IODA and Cloudflare Radar outage data and the PCH exchange directory.
